transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump / tub-to-pump hose. Next: Establish WHERE the water appears, WHEN in the cycle, and what it LOOKS like before choosing a part. Let me know what you find.

It's coming from the front of the machine, it started mid-wash today and it's still going. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now, is that ok?? I haven't touched the plug or turned anything off yet.
No, it is not safe to stand in water while an electrical appliance is running. Is the leaking water clean, soapy/dirty wash water, or dirty/oily-looking water?
It looks like normal soapy wash water, not oily or dirty. Should I go and turn it off at the fuse box now? The water has gone back towards the socket.

Yes, you should switch off the power immediately to prevent electric shock or fire hazards while standing on a wet floor. Do not touch any plugs or switches until the area is safe and dry. Next: If it started after cleaning the filter, re-seat the filter cap/seal and check the sealing face before suspecting the pump. Let me know what you find.
ok going to the fuse box in the hall now, the floor is dry there. Do I just switch the whole thing off? Then what do I do about the water?

Next: If the door seal is ripped, check the drum for up/down play, a dropped drum or bearing noise so a replacement seal isn't destroyed too. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I'm at the fuse box now, it didn't really answer me. Do I just switch the whole thing off? And then what do I do about the water, I've got towels?

Next: If there is a big leak with heavy banging, check for a loose counterweight / cracked tub. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'm at the fuse box and the assistant isn't answering my actual question. Do I just flip the main switch off? I'm really worried about the water by the socket, and I don't know what to do about the floor.

Yes, you should turn off the power at the mains to ensure safety while water is leaking near an electrical socket. Please do not touch any switches with wet hands and keep clear of the affected area until it is safe to proceed. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the pump filter cap or its seal. The pump filter cap at the bottom front is a common leak, especially if it's been opened recently. Check it's screwed in fully and straight, and that its rubber seal is clean. Was it loose or not seated, tight and dry already, or is the cap or seal cracked or damaged?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok, flipping the main switch off now. The filter cap is tight and the area behind the flap is dry, so it's not that. What do I do about the water on the floor?

From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
